[Hacker News — gist.github.com]
Tested on Linux, Claude Code 2.1.257–2.1.312 (see Tested versions). The binary is not modified ( BUN_OPTIONS=--preload ). An update can silently undo it, so see Verify.

curl -fsSL https://gist.githubusercontent.com/flamerix-ai/c3905705cc4205e5de3011fa2e74efce/raw/no-agent-summary.js -o ~ /.local/share/no-agent-summary.js claude daemon stop --any BUN_OPTIONS= " ${BUN_OPTIONS : + $BUN_OPTIONS } --preload $HOME /.local/share/no-agent-summary.js " claude To make it permanent for every Claude Code process, see Install .

Every ~30 seconds, for every background agent, Claude Code sends that agent's entire transcript to the agent's own model (usually Opus) and asks it to "describe your most recent action in 3-5 words". The answer only updates the agent's status line in the agents panel; it never reaches the model or your conversation. There is no setting that turns it off, and since 2.1.232 (August 2026) it has been on by default.

The anomaly was detected by DRIM in Claude Code's OpenTelemetry export: grouping claude_code.api_request events by query_source showed agent_summary costing more than the main conversation itself .

Spend here means Claude Code's own per-request estimate ( cost_usd ), not an invoice: on a subscription, what you lose is rate-limit headroom. We are not the only ones who measured it: #86879 collects four independent measurements of 18–26 %.

no-agent-summary.js is a Bun preload (~80 lines of code). It wraps setTimeout / setInterval ; when a callback's source text contains a summarizer anchor (e.g. the [AgentSummary] Timer fired log line), it returns an inert handle instead of arming the timer. Every other timer passes through untouched. In the OpenTelemetry export the suppressed requests are claude_code.api_request events with query_source = agent_summary .

Why a timer hook rather than something simpler: the module ships as precompiled Bun bytecode, so editing its JS text inside the binary changes nothing, and the API client does not go through a wrapped globalThis.fetch . But Function.prototype.toString still returns a callback's source even when it runs from bytecode, so the timer can be recognised by a string inside it. The inert timer uses exactly 2³¹−1 ms: Node and Bun treat a larger delay as 1 ms, so an "infinite" delay would fire at once.

Put no-agent-summary.js somewhere stable; note its absolute path.

Set BUN_OPTIONS globally so every Claude Code process gets it. One of:

# ~/.profile, ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc export BUN_OPTIONS= " ${BUN_OPTIONS : + $BUN_OPTIONS } --preload /abs/path/no-agent-summary.js " # ~/.config/fish/config.fish set -gx BUN_OPTIONS " --preload /abs/path/no-agent-summary.js " # ~/.config/environment.d/50-no-agent-summary.conf (systemd user env; also reaches # user services and timers; applies when the user manager next starts, usually next login) BUN_OPTIONS =--preload /abs/path/no-agent-summary.js Or a wrapper named claude earlier on PATH (the case keeps it idempotent when one Claude Code process starts another):

#! /bin/sh HOOK=/abs/path/no-agent-summary.js case " ${BUN_OPTIONS-} " in * " --preload $HOOK " * ) ;; * ) export BUN_OPTIONS= " ${BUN_OPTIONS : + $BUN_OPTIONS } --preload $HOOK " ;; esac : " ${CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_LOG := ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR :-/ tmp} / no-agent-summary.log} " export CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_LOG exec /path/to/the/real/claude " $@ " Restart the daemon and every already-running session, then start Claude Code from an environment that has BUN_OPTIONS :

claude daemon stop --any Env variable values effect CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_MODE off (default), pass off suppresses the summary timer. pass is the A/B control: loads and logs, arms every timer untouched. Any other value warns on stderr and acts as off . CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_LOG file path, optional Appends preload active mode=… bun=… hooked=… on load, one line per matched timer (first 20), and an exit count. CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_MARKER file path, optional Overwritten on load with the preload active … line. Nuances Restart the daemon after install. The daemon, pty host and pre-warmed bg-spare sessions inherit the environment of the client that started the daemon, so a daemon started before BUN_OPTIONS was set keeps spawning unhooked sessions. Hence claude daemon stop --any . Headless runs need it too: claude -p , cron, CI, editor integrations. Platform: Linux tested, macOS and Windows untested. On Windows the /$bunfs/ gate most likely never installs the hook. A/B: CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_MODE=pass loads the hook but arms every timer; the summaries come back, which shows the off result is the hook's doing. Background processes: daemon, pty host and bg-spare must carry --preload in their environment ( /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux); if not, restart the daemon. Verify (after every update) Preload loads:

BUN_OPTIONS= " --preload $HOME /.local/share/no-agent-summary.js " CC_AGENT_SUMMARY_LOG=/tmp/nas.log claude --version && cat /tmp/nas.log Expect preload active mode=off … . No line: BUN_OPTIONS did not reach the process, or the p
reactions: [Hacker News] That was my experience in the Opus 4.5 - 4.7 era, but recently it's been on the nose with what I want it to carry over, or close enough that a full handoff would be more expensive than just letting it find what it needs again. I'm mostly working on moderately sized rust codebases (600k~ lines) with reasonably long running tasks. The only time I intentionally do a handoff is if the next g

[Hacker News] For certain workloads compaction is great, for others you're better off manually doing a /handoff (or a similar skill you write yourself to keep what you need, toss what you don't; Claude is not always good at figuring it out). Read your memory.md to see what Claude thinks is very important.

[Hacker News] of course it does, that's the point of it. The notable discovery here isn't that the AI agent has access to its own transcript, it's that 20% extra tokens are used to generate the status line. Leave it to LLM writing to focus on something inconsequential though.

[Hacker News] If they are literally sending the entire transcript and asking for a summary, wouldn't almost all of the tokens be cache hit? Maybe. But the 16.4% is from Claude Code's own cost_usd estimate, so cheap per token still adds up when it's 1 in 5 requests.

[Hacker News] I have not. Obviously YMMV, but tools have ~8k tokens of descriptions of their own, including (imo too much) behavioural guidance. The tool descriptions are retained with `--system-prompt ""`, I'm sure you can get Claude to output what's in there exactly as it changes quite a lot between versions.

[Hacker News] The newer the CC cli is, the more tokens it burns. I use a very old version and killed its "no matter what I'm still gonna autoupdate myself to the latest version", because new ones do all kinds of useless tasks in the background. If you are on a tight budget use an older version (1+ year) of the cc cli, and it saves you a lot of money.

items.title: Claude Code regularly sends each background agent’s transcript to its model
